title: Power Pages: transfer site ownership from the Power Platform admin center
summary: The transfer route, role conditions, audit operation and roadmap details are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting ownership wording in the roles documentation and remove checklist instructions for configuring controls that the table only describes how to view.

claims.claim: The roadmap says existing site owners and global administrators can assign an eligible site's ownership to another valid tenant user.
claims.quote: Existing site owners and global administrators can assign ownership to another valid user within the tenant

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: The roadmap says ownership transfer does not require a support request.
claims.quote: without requiring manual intervention from support.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The general availability target is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The preview target is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The record lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The record lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The record lists the Web platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Why it matters
claims.claim: The roadmap says the capability is enabled automatically for admins, makers and marketers.
claims.quote: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

claims.claim: The transfer capability is on when it arrives, rather than requiring an administrator to enable its availability.
claims.quote: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

claims.claim: The transfer control is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Power Pages > site > Site Details > Edit > Owner.
claims.quote: select Manage, and then select Power Pages. ... Select the Power Pages site that you want to update. ... On the Site Details page, select Edit. ... In the Owner field, remove the current owner and search for the new owner.

claims.claim: The procedure ends with a confirmation message and the Transfer button.
claims.quote: Review the confirmation message, and then select Transfer.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The selected user becomes the site's primary owner when the transfer finishes.
claims.quote: When the transfer finishes, the selected user becomes the primary owner of the site.
claims.fix: After this sentence add: 'The roles page still describes the website owner as the creator and says that ownership cannot be transferred or changed; Microsoft has not reconciled that wording with the transfer procedure.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/admin-roles#website-owner, which says 'ownership remains with the creator and can't be transferred or changed.' Do not infer that the different ownership terms are equivalent.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap describes a Power Advisor view identifying sites without a valid owner.
claims.quote: Power Pages also identifies sites that no longer have a valid owner and surfaces this information on Power Advisor.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview exposes the Transfer site ownership activity under operation OwnershipTransferred.
claims.quote: Transfer site ownership | OwnershipTransferred | Ownership of the site is transferred to another user.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not document transfer notifications at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages transfer site ownership notification email eligible sites tenant disable automatic reassignment. Opened transfer-ownership and admin-roles; neither documents transfer notifications. Search results about ownership emails concern SharePoint, not Power Pages.

claims.claim: The security recommendations documentation describes a valid-owner recommendation for apps.
claims.quote: This type of recommendation lists apps in all the managed environments within your Power Platform tenant that don't have a valid owner.

claims.claim: The Sites security recommendations cover WAF, SSL certificates and authentication keys.
claims.quote: Enable Web Application Firewall (WAF) to protect websites ... Enhance your website's security by renewing its SSL certificate ... Ensure uninterrupted access to your websites by renewing their authentication key

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not document the roadmap's Power Advisor recommendation for Power Pages sites without valid owners.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Advisor Power Pages sites no valid owner recommendation. Opened security-recommendations and power-platform-advisor; read action-center and Power Pages inventory excerpts. Ownerless-app recommendations and site inventory do not document the claimed site-owner recommendation.

claims.claim: The roles documentation requires website app ownership for managing a website authentication key.
claims.quote: Manage authentication key | Website app owner and any one of the following roles:

claims.claim: The roles page requires direct assignment of admin roles for tasks requiring those roles.
claims.quote: To perform a task, which requires an admin role, a user must be directly assigned to the required role.

claims.claim: The roles page says these admin roles are not inherited from security group membership.
claims.quote: These roles aren't inherited from security group membership or through privileged identity management (PIM).

claims.claim: The roles page says these admin roles are not inherited through privileged identity management.
claims.quote: These roles aren't inherited from security group membership or through privileged identity management (PIM).

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope
claims.claim: The Power Pages activity-log prerequisites require configuring and enabling auditing for the production environments being monitored.
claims.quote: Configure and turn on auditing for the Power Platform production environments you want to monitor

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Viewing Power Pages audit activity requires the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: assign either the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role in Microsoft Purview to you.

claims.claim: The audit solution is at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Audit.
claims.quote: On the left navigation pane, select Solutions and then select Audit.

claims.claim: Exchange Online PowerShell supports Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate $start -EndDate $end -Operations OwnershipTransferred to search the transfer operation.
claims.quote: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -EndDate <ExDateTime> -StartDate <ExDateTime> ... [-Operations <String[]>] ... The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation.

claims.claim: The Power Pages activity-log page names OwnershipTransferred but does not name Search-UnifiedAuditLog.
claims.quote: Searched the fetched activity-logs-power-pages page for Search-UnifiedAuditLog and read its complete Access the logs section and activity table. It documents OwnershipTransferred, the Purview search UI and the Office 365 Management API, but not that cmdlet.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The documented transfer is a manual per-site procedure initiated by an administrator, not an automatic transfer on rollout.
claims.quote: Select the Power Pages site that you want to update. ... In the Owner field, remove the current owner and search for the new owner. ... Review the confirmation message, and then select Transfer.

claims.claim: Learn does not document automated reassignment through this site ownership transfer procedure.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages transfer site ownership impact visitors end users eligibility notification automatic reassignment. Read transfer-ownership in full and the Websites and CLI operations. No automatic execution of the documented transfer procedure was described.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not document an API or command equivalent to the admin-centre ownership transfer itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages transfer ownership API pac pages admin PowerShell Dataverse website ownerid. Read admin-api, Websites, pac pages/power-pages and powerpagesite: Site record Assign is documented, but no text identifies it as equivalent to the admin-centre transfer.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The transfer page lists roles, admin centre access and the new owner's user type as prerequisites without naming a licence.
claims.quote: You are the website app owner and have any one of the following roles ... You have access to the Power Platform admin center. ... The new owner is an enabled Microsoft Entra user with a Member user type.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The add-on licensing model reflects the documented Power Pages monthly capacity add-ons for external users.
claims.quote: Power Pages is licensed by using authenticated user monthly capacity and anonymous user monthly capacity add-ons for external users.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Authenticated user monthly capacity is a Power Pages add-on for external users.
claims.quote: Power Pages is licensed by using authenticated user monthly capacity and anonymous user monthly capacity add-ons for external users.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Anonymous user monthly capacity is a Power Pages add-on for external users.
claims.quote: Power Pages is licensed by using authenticated user monthly capacity and anonymous user monthly capacity add-ons for external users.

claims.claim: A meter specific to site ownership transfer is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages site ownership transfer pricing licensing fee meter. Read transfer-ownership, website-consumption-reports and licensing FAQ/pay-as-you-go meter search excerpts. The documented site usage meters count users, not ownership transfers.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A price or charge specific to site ownership transfers is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages site ownership transfer pricing licensing fee meter. Read transfer-ownership and website-consumption-reports; reviewed licensing FAQ and pay-as-you-go meter excerpts. No transfer-specific price was stated.

claims.claim: A licence condition specific to ownership transfer is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages site ownership transfer pricing licensing fee meter. Read transfer-ownership prerequisites and website-consumption-reports, plus product licensing FAQ excerpts. None states a licence condition specific to transferring ownership.

claims.claim: The actions page analyses managed environments, and access to recommendation details and actions can depend on Managed Environments being enabled.
claims.quote: All the recommendations, affected resource details, and actions are available for the managed environments in your tenant. The actions page shows a summary of recommendations for non-managed environments.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap nor Learn defines which site characteristics make a site eligible or ineligible for this transfer.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "ownership transfer" "eligible"; Power Pages transfer site ownership impact visitors end users eligibility notification automatic reassignment. Read roadmap, transfer-ownership and admin-roles; found user prerequisites but no site eligibility definition.

claims.claim: There is no documented tenant-wide on/off switch for this transfer capability in the controls described.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer tenant setting disable transfer ownership. Read transfer-ownership and admin-api; reviewed tenant site-creation and site-visibility results. Those settings govern creation or visibility, not ownership transfer.

claims.claim: The Power Pages activity-log page documents developer access to the logs through the Office 365 Management API.
claims.quote: The logs are also accessible to developers via the Office 365 Management API.

claims.claim: Learn advises verifying that the new owner can access and manage the site.
claims.quote: Verify that the new owner can access and manage the site.

claims.claim: The roadmap and transfer documentation do not describe an effect on site visitors.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages transfer site ownership impact visitors end users eligibility notification automatic reassignment. Read the roadmap and transfer-ownership in full; neither describes a visitor-facing change from ownership transfer.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, auditing and role-assignment bullet
claims.claim: The audit row supplies the controls that the checklist tells readers to configure.
claims.quote: Turn on auditing for the production environments ... assign the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role ... (Purview audit row). The row instead gives Solutions > Audit and Search-UnifiedAuditLog.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet beginning 'Turn on auditing for the production environments'. It instructs readers to enable environment auditing and assign audit roles, neither of which has a configuration row; the existing audit row only searches activity. Retain the verified prerequisites in the row note and Scope. Do not add rows as part of this correction.

claims.claim: For sites outside the managed identity model, a missing ownership transfer option can indicate that the administrator is not the web app owner.
claims.quote: For other portals, if you don't see the ownership transfer option, check whether you're the web app owner.

claims.claim: Access to the Power Platform admin center is a transfer prerequisite.
claims.quote: You have access to the Power Platform admin center.
